skills.name: huggingface-local-models
skills.purpose: Finds llama.cpp-compatible GGUF repos on the Hugging Face Hub, picks the right quant for the machine (CPU, Mac Metal, CUDA, ROCm) and launches the model with llama-cli or llama-server as an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint. Converts Transformers weights to GGUF only when no GGUF exists.
skills.how_to_use: Add the marketplace (`/plugin marketplace add huggingface/skills`), then `hf skills add huggingface-local-models`. Triggers on running a model locally, GGUF or llama.cpp. Needs llama.cpp (brew/winget or a source build) and `hf auth login` for gated repos.
skills.evidence: Official Hugging Face; huggingface/skills 11.1k stars; skills.sh ~1.6k installs; added Apr 2026; uses the Hub's own `?local-app=llama.cpp` quant recommendations; re-hosted in sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills.
skills.notes: References cover Hub discovery, quant tables with imatrix, and Metal/CUDA/ROCm builds.

skills.name: hf-cli
skills.purpose: Teaches the agent every `hf` command for the Hugging Face Hub: search, download and upload models and datasets, manage the local cache and auth, repos, discussions, Spaces, buckets and HF Jobs.
skills.how_to_use: `/plugin marketplace add huggingface/skills` then `/plugin install hf-cli@huggingface/skills`. Needs the `hf` CLI (huggingface_hub; pip/uv or the official installer). Run `hf auth login` for gated or private repos.
skills.evidence: Official Hugging Face; most-installed HF skill on skills.sh (~3.0k); the README calls it the recommended first skill; generated from huggingface_hub v2.1.1 and updated 1 Oct 2026; also in the Cursor and Codex plugin directories.
skills.notes: Its install line is Hugging Face's own official installer piped to the shell (`curl -LsSf https://hf.co/cli/install.sh | bash -s`); `pip install -U huggingface_hub` is the alternative. Jobs and buckets are paid HF features.

skills.name: huggingface-llm-trainer
skills.purpose: Fine-tunes language and vision models with TRL or Unsloth on Hugging Face Jobs cloud GPUs (SFT, DPO, GRPO, reward modelling). Covers dataset validation, hardware choice and cost estimates, Trackio monitoring, saving to the Hub and GGUF conversion for local use.
skills.how_to_use: `hf skills add huggingface-llm-trainer` after the hf-cli plugin. Triggers on training or fine-tuning without a local GPU. Needs an HF write token and an account plan that allows Jobs.
skills.evidence: Official Hugging Face; skills.sh ~2.0k installs (plus ~430 under its earlier name hugging-face-model-trainer); mirrored by patchy631/ai-engineering-hub; updated Jul 2026.
skills.notes: HF Jobs need a paid Pro, Team or Enterprise plan (cost table about $1-20 per run). One dataset-inspector helper runs a script from an HF staff member's dataset repo (evalstate/trl-helpers) on huggingface.co.

skills.name: trl-training
skills.purpose: Writing and debugging post-training code with TRL: picks the right Trainer/Config pair (SFT, DPO, GRPO, KTO, reward model, on-policy distillation), the matching dataset format, the trl CLI and common pitfalls.
skills.how_to_use: Copy the folder from the TRL repo or `hf skills add trl-training`. Triggers on TRL Python API or `trl` CLI work. Needs `pip install trl` and a GPU for real runs.
skills.evidence: Official, kept inside the TRL repo (huggingface/trl, 19.4k stars) and mirrored byte-for-byte in huggingface/skills (skills.sh ~800 installs); updated 1 Oct 2026.
skills.notes: Short router (4 KB) that points to the TRL docs for each trainer; pair with huggingface-llm-trainer to run it on HF Jobs.

skills.name: llamafactory-sft
skills.purpose: A guided end-to-end LlamaFactory fine-tune: data prep, model download, choosing LoRA/QLoRA/full and the config, background training, loss plots, checking the result and exporting the model. It asks the user at each decision point.
skills.how_to_use: Works when Claude Code runs inside a LlamaFactory checkout (`pip install -e .`, `llamafactory-cli`). Triggers when the user wants to fine-tune or SFT a model with LlamaFactory.
skills.evidence: Official, shipped inside LlamaFactory (hiyouga/LlamaFactory, 75.3k stars); listed on skillsmp; 35 KB workflow with a progress board. Orchestra's shorter llama-factory skill (~860 installs) covers the same tool.
skills.notes: Expects a local NVIDIA/Ascend GPU or similar; the repo also ships llamafactory-v1-docs.

skills.name: diffusers-cli
skills.purpose: Runs open image and video diffusion pipelines (FLUX, Wan, HunyuanVideo and any other DiffusionPipeline) from the terminal with `diffusers-cli`: one-off or batch generation, printing a pipeline's input schema without downloading weights, attaching LoRAs at inference and environment checks.
skills.how_to_use: Copy the folder from the diffusers repo. Needs a recent `pip install diffusers` plus torch and a GPU. `--remote` runs the same command on HF Jobs (paid).
skills.evidence: Official, shipped in huggingface/diffusers (34.6k stars) under .ai/skills; listed on skillsmp and skills.sh (new, few installs).
skills.notes: Lives in the repo's contributor-facing .ai folder next to model-integration and custom-blocks skills. Check each model's weight licence before shipping outputs (e.g. FLUX.1-dev is non-commercial).

skills.name: comfyui
skills.purpose: Drives ComfyUI to generate images, video and audio with open diffusion models (SD/SDXL, FLUX, SD3, Wan, HunyuanVideo). Checks hardware, installs and launches ComfyUI, reads a workflow's controllable parameters, finds missing nodes and models, then submits and downloads results over the REST/WebSocket API.
skills.how_to_use: Copy the folder (it is an optional Hermes Agent skill). Run `scripts/hardware_check.py` first, then `scripts/comfyui_setup.sh` for a local install, or use a Comfy Cloud API key. Needs Python; comfy-cli is installed via pipx/uvx.
skills.evidence: NousResearch/hermes-agent (251k stars) optional skill, v5.1.0 with tests and workflow templates; skills.sh ~390 installs; listed on skillsmp. Not ranked in image_creation, which has Hermes's separate stable-diffusion skill.
skills.notes: Setup turns comfy-cli analytics off (`comfy --skip-prompt tracking disable`). The optional Comfy Cloud route sends prompts to cloud.comfy.org, ComfyUI's own host.

skills.name: runpod
skills.purpose: Entry point for Runpod GPU hosting. It routes to the right lane: GPU pods, serverless endpoints, Flash (write Python locally, run it on remote GPUs), templates such as ComfyUI or vLLM, network volumes and the runpodctl CLI. It indexes about two dozen verified end-to-end examples, including fine-tune to serverless and a Whisper endpoint.
skills.how_to_use: `/plugin marketplace add runpod/runpod-plugins-official` then `/plugin install runpod@runpod` (or `npx skills add runpod/runpod-plugins-official`). Needs a Runpod account and API key. The hosted Runpod MCP server is optional.
skills.evidence: Official Runpod marketplace; skills.sh ~8.8k installs for this router (runpodctl ~10.5k, flash ~10.1k, companion-clis ~9.8k); updated 28 Sep 2026.
skills.notes: Paid GPUs. The runpodctl skill offers Runpod's own installer piped to the shell (`curl -sSL https://cli.runpod.net | bash`) beside `brew install runpod/runpodctl/runpodctl`.

skills.name: gguf-quantization
skills.purpose: GGUF and llama.cpp quantization: choosing K-quants from Q2_K to Q8_0, building imatrix quants, converting HF models, and running them on CPU, Apple Silicon or consumer GPUs with Ollama, LM Studio or llama-cpp-python. Also says when AWQ, GPTQ, HQQ or bitsandbytes fit better.
skills.how_to_use: `npx @orchestra-research/ai-research-skills` (interactive installer) or copy the folder. Triggers on quantizing or deploying models on consumer hardware. Needs llama.cpp or llama-cpp-python.
skills.evidence: Orchestra-Research/AI-Research-SKILLs (13.2k stars); skills.sh ~890 installs; aitmpl ~45 downloads (as optimization-gguf); mirrored in davila7/claude-code-templates and Hermes.
skills.notes: Sibling skills in the same repo cover awq, gptq, hqq and bitsandbytes when GPU-serving quantization is needed.

skills.name: huggingface-best
skills.purpose: Answers 'which model should I use for X on my machine'. It queries Hugging Face's official benchmark leaderboards for the task, adds parameter counts, filters by what fits the user's RAM or VRAM (fp16 vs Q4 budgets) and returns a comparison table.
skills.how_to_use: `hf skills add huggingface-best`. Triggers on 'best model for', 'what model runs on my laptop', 'compare models'. Uses curl and jq against huggingface.co, with the HF token if present.
skills.evidence: Official Hugging Face; skills.sh ~1.6k installs; updated Aug 2026.
skills.notes: Benchmark-based only; pair with open-weights for the licence check. Calls only huggingface.co.

skills.name: lora-qlora-recipes
skills.purpose: Current best-practice LoRA and QLoRA settings for supervised fine-tuning: rank, alpha, target modules, learning rates, and when to choose LoRA, QLoRA or a full fine-tune.
skills.how_to_use: `/plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents` then `/plugin install llm-finetuning`. Triggers when writing or reviewing a LoRA/QLoRA training config.
skills.evidence: wshobson/agents (40.2k stars) llm-finetuning plugin, added Jul 2026; skills.sh ~2.1k installs. The same plugin has finetuning-method-selection, quantized-export (merged vs LoRA-only, GGUF with imatrix, AWQ, FP8; ~2.1k installs each) and eval-harness-first.
skills.notes: Library-agnostic advice; use with trl-training, unsloth-buddy or llamafactory-sft to actually run.

skills.name: modal
skills.purpose: Runs Python on Modal's serverless GPUs: images, GPU selection, volumes, secrets, web endpoints, scheduled and batch jobs, and serving or fine-tuning open models without managing servers.
skills.how_to_use: `npx skills add K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills` (or copy the folder). Needs `pip install modal`, a Modal account and token (`modal setup`), plus a payment method for GPU use.
skills.evidence: K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills (47.5k stars); skills.sh ~1.7k installs; on aitmpl; reviewed against Modal SDK 1.6.0. Orchestra's modal-serverless-gpu (~860 installs) is the alternative.
skills.notes: No official Modal Labs skill was found. Paid service; GPU use needs a payment method even with credits.

skills.name: vllm-deploy-simple
skills.purpose: Installs vLLM for the detected backend (NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, TPU or CPU) in a venv, starts an OpenAI-compatible server for a chosen model and smoke-tests `/v1/models` and chat completions.
skills.how_to_use: Add `vllm-project/vllm-skills` as a Claude Code plugin marketplace and install the vllm-skills plugin. Run `scripts/quickstart.sh --model <hf-id> --port 8000`. Needs Python 3.10+ and uv or pip.
skills.evidence: Official vLLM project; skills.sh ~200 installs (sibling skills: deploy-docker ~230, deploy-k8s ~160, bench-serve ~200). Orchestra's serving-llms-vllm (~950 installs) adds production tuning (PagedAttention, quantized serving).
skills.notes: The quickstart script only talks to localhost. For Docker, Kubernetes and benchmarking use the sibling skills in the same plugin.

skills.name: evaluating-llms-harness
skills.purpose: Benchmarks open models with EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness across 60+ tasks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA). Covers HF Transformers and vLLM backends, few-shot settings and tracking results during training.
skills.how_to_use: `npx @orchestra-research/ai-research-skills` or copy the folder. Needs `pip install lm-eval` and a GPU for larger models.
skills.evidence: Orchestra (13.2k stars); skills.sh ~880 installs; the most-downloaded ai-research skill on aitmpl (~85); mirrored in Hermes and davila7.
skills.notes: Academic benchmarks; for task-specific golden sets see wshobson's eval-harness-first.

skills.name: huggingface-community-evals
skills.purpose: Runs evaluations of Hub models on local hardware with inspect-ai or lighteval, including picking vLLM, Transformers or accelerate as the backend, smoke tests and fallbacks.
skills.how_to_use: `hf skills add huggingface-community-evals`. Uses the bundled scripts; needs a local GPU and Python. Hands off to the HF Jobs skill to run the same eval remotely.
skills.evidence: Official Hugging Face; skills.sh ~1.7k installs.
skills.notes: Runs evals locally only; publishing results to model cards is out of scope.

skills.name: open-weights
skills.purpose: Chooses an open-weight model and checks whether it can be used. Five gates in order: task fit, size versus hardware, licence class (OSI-open vs custom community vs non-commercial), hardware target and community support. Rule: always verify the licence on the model card.
skills.how_to_use: `npx @ericrisco/rsc@latest onboard` installs the harness, or copy the folder. Triggers on 'which open model', 'can I ship this model commercially', and model sizing. It does not download or run anything.
skills.evidence: ericrisco/rsc-harness (142 stars, created May 2026, 270 skills, each with evals). The only substantive skill found that centres on clearing open-weight licences. It cites verified mid-2026 licence changes (Gemma 4 to Apache-2.0, Codestral 2, DeepSeek-V3 custom vs R1 MIT).
skills.notes: Low stars and installs (skills.sh ~3), but fills the licence gap in this craft. Its model and licence lists are dated mid-2026, and it says so itself.

skills.name: ollama
skills.purpose: Runs open-weight LLMs on one machine with Ollama: pull and tag models, the native and OpenAI-compatible APIs on localhost:11434, Modelfiles, picking Q4_K_M/Q8_0/fp16, sizing VRAM and RAM, and recognising when a model belongs on a remote GPU instead.
skills.how_to_use: Install via `npx @ericrisco/rsc@latest onboard` or copy the folder. Needs Ollama installed from ollama.com. `scripts/verify.sh` checks that app code points at the local endpoint.
skills.evidence: ericrisco/rsc-harness (142 stars). Ollama has no official skill (ollama/ollama ships none). Chosen over BagelHole/DevOps-Security-Agent-Skills ollama-stack (1.1k stars, thinner, with Open WebUI; skills.sh ~290) and luongnv89 ollama-optimizer (129 stars, hardware tuning); both were reviewed.
skills.notes: References cover the API, hardware sizing, licences and model families. The skill itself pipes nothing to a shell.

skills.name: swift-mlx-lm
skills.purpose: Runs LLMs and VLMs on Apple Silicon with MLX Swift LM: local inference and streaming, wired-memory coordination, KV cache, tool calling, embeddings, LoRA fine-tuning and porting new models.
skills.how_to_use: Symlink `skills/mlx-swift-lm` into `~/.claude/skills/` (per the repo's skills/README). For Swift apps on macOS or iOS; needs Xcode/SwiftPM and an Apple Silicon Mac.
skills.evidence: Official ml-explore (Apple MLX team) repo, pushed 3 Oct 2026; skills.sh ~18 installs (a community copy, PicoMLX/mlx-swift-lm-skill, has ~30).
skills.notes: Swift only. No strong skill was found for the Python mlx-lm CLI (awni/mlx-skills fast-mlx is about optimising MLX code; huggingface/transformers-to-mlx has no licence).

skills.name: unsloth-buddy
skills.purpose: A guided Unsloth fine-tuning companion: interviews the user, detects the environment, then runs SFT, DPO, GRPO, ORPO, KTO or SimPO with LoRA, plus vision, TTS and embedding fine-tunes. Includes VRAM optimisation, a live training dashboard, evaluation, GGUF export via llama.cpp, and an MLX route on Apple Silicon.
skills.how_to_use: `/plugin marketplace add TYH-labs/unsloth-buddy` then `/plugin install unsloth-buddy@TYH-labs/unsloth-buddy`. Install the whole repo because it uses sub-skills and scripts. NVIDIA GPU with CUDA, or Apple Silicon with mlx-tune, or Colab.
skills.evidence: TYH-labs/unsloth-buddy (280 stars, Mar 2026); a Claude Code plugin and Gemini extension with its own eval suite. Unsloth has no official agent skill (unslothai/unsloth bundles only a skill-creator); Orchestra's unsloth skill is a 2 KB stub plus references.
skills.notes: Install option B pipes Unsloth's own auto-install helper to Python (`wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unslothai/unsloth/main/unsloth/_auto_install.py | python -`); this is the vendor's script, offered as one option. The Apple Silicon route uses the third-party mlx-tune package. A demo-design helper downloads templates from unpkg.com (download only).

skills.name: h3lite
skills.purpose: Turns a Windows + NVIDIA PC into a local MiniMax H3 audio-video workstation through ComfyUI. It reads the hardware, chooses component set, resolution and time budget, runs doctor and preflight checks, generates clips with low-VRAM routes, and repairs broken installs.
skills.how_to_use: Copy the repo as a skill (it targets Codex and Claude-style agents). Needs Windows, an NVIDIA GPU with about 8-16 GB VRAM, and ComfyUI. macOS and Linux are marked experimental.
skills.evidence: Fast-rising: 452 stars in about 7 weeks since 13 Aug 2026, riding the open-weight MiniMax H3 video model release (MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3, 9.5k stars, created 30 Jul 2026; its h3-prompt-writing skill has ~9.8k skills.sh installs). h3lite itself has ~17 skills.sh installs.
skills.notes: link-only (security): the preferred install route has the user download a packaged bundle of model files AND ComfyUI custom_nodes (executable code) from Baidu Netdisk share links and merge it into ComfyUI. Upstream sources with hashes are only the fallback. Only Windows + NVIDIA is validated. Check the H3 weight licence on the model card.
